features.title: Hot reload and closure identity
features.gap: Luau upvalue identity is approximate (Luau has no lua_upvalueid, so shared scalar aliases cannot be proven - an explicit capability boundary, not a fixable bug). Delivered this round: failed reload rollback. reload_modules is a two-phase commit with a strong-reference shallow snapshot taken before any write, new modules computed in the sandbox without touching old objects, an xpcall-wrapped commit, and rollback of the module table / package.loaded / loaded_modules / loaded_module_times on failure; module_loaded hooks fire only after a successful commit; update_global's registry scan is pcall-guarded so the Luau debug.getregistry shim can no longer abort a whole reload. M.reload and reload_modules return ok, err, the no-argument path advances loaded_module_times only after success so a failed reload stays retryable, and Lua.HotReload() now surfaces that boolean. Rollback is explicitly best-effort, not a transaction: _G, live stack locals, arbitrary tables/upvalues and the registry are not snapshotted.
features.acceptance: Test shared closures, table cycles, delegates, active coroutine and failed reload rollback; RuntimeModules.spec.cpp now drives success, load-time error, and syntax-error + no-argument retry paths entirely in memory through an injected package.searchers source switch on both backends. A real file-mtime / multi-module / active-coroutine reload run is still pending.

features.title: Declared server/client/multicast RPC
features.gap: Sorted registration, whole-RPC parameter validation, reliable/unreliable flags on all three kinds, and parent-class schema lookup delivered. RPC parameters accept any resolvable UScriptStruct and Array/Set/Map nests: the runtime-built UFunction gains a real FStructProperty/FArrayProperty/FSetProperty/FMapProperty, and the peer declaration report exports the FProperty-derived spec of every parameter (not an echo of the Lua script), so a connected gate can prove the property was actually built. The engine already rejects a non-owner Server RPC (UNetDriver::ShouldCallRemoteFunction requires RepFlags.bNetOwner); the DS scenario and release gate assert this with a unique token, but that assertion has not been executed. Eight opt-in connected scenarios (late join, process-level reconnect, dormancy, relevancy, join-order swap, packet loss, UNetConnection-level reconnect, cross-peer schema fingerprint) and four delivery variants (Legacy/PushOff/Iris/Cooked) are delivered in source with fail-closed gates, but none has been executed. No further source gap is claimed; the remaining work is execution only.
features.acceptance: The connected DS + 2 clients scenario includes an explicit non-owner Server RPC rejection assertion (unique token, exact CallLog comparison, and a ValidateRelease.py gate requiring the attempt itself). Late join needs a spawn marker plus topology launch order; the swapped-order scenario needs the reverse; reconnect needs a distinct replacement PID and launch_count=2; UNetConnection-level reconnect needs launch_count=1, a closed connection address and an in-process reopen; packet loss needs real NetEmulation plus convergence of the final field value; schema mismatch needs identical RepSchemaVersion on all three peers plus a discriminating VariantRepSchemaVersion. Cooked needs a staged WindowsServer/Windows peer exe and a WITH_EDITOR-derived flag. All of these must be executed via Tools/RunNetMatrix.ps1 before they count. Reliable/unreliable, declaration syntax, spec parsing and UStruct property construction are covered by unit cases.

features.title: Property conditions and schemas
features.gap: One storage group per supported condition (None/InitialOnly/OwnerOnly/SkipOwner/SimulatedOnly/AutonomousOnly/SimulatedOrPhysics/InitialOrOwner), plus a shared Generic group for arbitrary UStruct/container fields; malformed and unsupported declarations (Custom/Dynamic/Never/NetGroup/Replay*) are rejected atomically and cached schemas stay immutable. A subclass without its own declaration inherits the parent's schema. Multi-Env joint ownership is now fixed: identical declarations bound by several environments are released only when the last one closes, in any order (previously closing the first owner wiped a schema another Env still used), and weak UObject references that have gone invalid never write a stale pointer back to Lua. Both have dedicated unit cases. The connected declaration report exports TypeSpec, RepSchemaVersion and a deliberately different VariantRepSchemaVersion from every peer, so a mismatched declaration cannot decode into the wrong slot. Connected owner/non-owner visibility, dormancy, relevancy, join-order swaps and packet-loss convergence are asserted by scenario source and gates, but none has been executed. No further source gap is claimed.
features.acceptance: The per-condition layout is delivered, and the DS scenario source mixes unconditional, OwnerOnly and Generic fields in one declaration list and exports per-peer visibility, TypeSpec, RPC parameter specs and declaration fingerprints for ValidateRelease.py to assert. Dormancy requires a client to observe a suppressed dormant value and then the flushed value; relevancy requires the non-owner to lose the owner-only actor; packet loss requires replication to converge under NetEmulation. All of these must be executed before they count.

features.title: Replication types, UStruct/containers and Iris/push model
features.gap: Strict int32/int64 conversion, scalar and Object bucket round-trips, invalid weak objects, and per-condition storage covered by unit cases. The earlier claim that arbitrary UStruct/container fields are an architecture boundary was wrong: a UClass cannot gain a UPROPERTY at runtime, but a generic bucket carrying a canonical self-describing payload does not need one, and a runtime-built UFunction can own any FStructProperty/FArrayProperty/FSetProperty/FMapProperty. Both paths are delivered, with the spec folded into SchemaVersion so mismatched peers cannot misdecode. UObject references keep the dedicated Object bucket because a text payload cannot carry a NetGUID. The Legacy / PushOff / Iris / Cooked delivery matrix, eight connected scenarios and Tools/RunNetMatrix.ps1 are delivered in source; AppendWorldFacts exports real NetEmulation state, Iris/push-model cvars, WITH_EDITOR and UNetConnection byte/loss counters so an Iris element-level delta comparison can be made from the reports. No variant or scenario has been executed, and no compression win is claimed.
features.acceptance: ValidateRelease.py --net-matrix must see four variant topologies (including a staged WindowsServer/Windows peer exe for Cooked) and eight scenario topologies, each with real engine switch state, cooked flag, declaration fingerprints, Generic field/RPC parameter specs and non-zero connection byte counters read back from every peer. Exact integer boundaries, Object resolution/invalidation, multi-Env teardown order, spec parsing/nesting and canonical Lua <-> payload round-trips are covered by unit cases.

features.title: Readonly globals, threads and class tables
features.gap: Capability trimming delivered: lua.sandboxdeny removes named globals before luaL_sandbox freezes _G, protects host-written globals (UE.*/Lua/package.loaded/require) and returns the removal count so a spec can tell 'policy applied' from a no-op. features.title: Host module loader versus upstream Require
features.gap: Host searchers/preload still differ from upstream Require config semantics. Delivered: relative-path mangling fixed (LoadFromFileSystem only rewrites dots for dotted module names, so './Foo' / 'Foo.lua' / explicit paths keep their dots), package.aliases redirects require on both backends via a searcher placed before preload (alias and target share one cached module instance, self-aliases raise instead of recursing), and the Luau-side FLuaEnv::Require now detects cyclic dependencies with a dedicated 'loading' upvalue - it names the module in the error and clears the marks on success and failure so one failed load cannot poison later requires. Delivered this round: a require-wrapper cycle guard installed after HotReload replaces _G.require, so named cycle detection covers plain Lua's native require, FLuaEnv::Require and HotReload's replacement at once without changing loader signatures or the compiled chunks that HotReload applies setfenv/_ENV to (wrapping searchers would have defeated that); unrequire(name) clears package.loaded and HotReload's three private caches while keeping package.preload and package.aliases declarations, reloadmodule(name) is unrequire + require, and package.resolution() declares the case, cooked, @alias-config, cycle and unload contract in machine-readable form. A leading '@' now fails with an explicit unsupported-@alias-config-files error, and lua.requireresolution adds opt-in unresolved-path diagnostics. Upstream @alias config files remain deliberately unsupported; case-insensitive fallback is explicitly out of scope and a real cooked-build resolution run is still pending.
features.acceptance: Document resolution/cycle/cache contract and add case/cook tests or explicit unsupported errors; LuaEnv.spec.cpp and LuauIntegration.spec.cpp cover alias redirection, self-alias rejection, cycle rejection and post-failure reuse; ModuleContracts.spec.cpp now covers the wrapped require cycle guard, argument/return pass-through, unrequire/reloadmodule, package.resolution and the @alias refusal on both backends. A real cooked-build and case-sensitive-filesystem resolution run is still pending.

features.title: Coverage export and quality gates
features.gap: Exported and gated: per-line Luau counters, declared exclusions, recomputed totals, multi-run aggregation and fail-closed coverage thresholds. Source names come from reachable global/module tables rather than a source map; C closures have no counters; chunks loaded before luau.coverage was set carry none, and only the Luau backend can export.
features.acceptance: lua.coverage dump writes per-source line counters; Tools/ValidateCoverage.py recomputes totals, merges runs by max hits, requires named sources and a threshold, and fails on missing, empty, level-0 or mismatched reports. 15 tooling regressions pass without UE; execution evidence still requires a real run.

features.acceptance: Record flags, compatibility/ABI/type declarations and tests before exposing as stable.

features.title: debug, upvalues and uservalues
features.gap: Exact subset delivered and documented: debug.getregistry rejects explicitly instead of returning a misleading empty table; getuservalue is the documented nil-only subset HotReload.lua relies on; setuservalue returns false instead of a pretend success; upvalueid is value identity (exact for shared references, slot identity for scalars, never a scalar-aliasing proof). Backend-specific spec cases cover all four. Full Lua 5.x debug parity is not claimed.
features.acceptance: Reject unsupported operations or implement exact subset; test closure identity and error cases. Both backends must keep their own exact semantics (Luau compat layer vs plain Lua native debug table).

features.title: Optional rooted buffered io
features.gap: Delivered: CRLF/path/read checks, strict mode validation (r/w/a/+/b, unknown or empty modes refused), strict seek whence ('set'/'cur'/'end', clamped to the in-memory buffer), format lists for file:lines() and io.lines() (shared reader for 'a'/'l'/'L'/'n' and numeric counts), a lua.iomaxbytes quota on open/write/flush, writes that overwrite at __pos and advance the position (append mode still forces the end), an in-memory io.tmpfile() whose flush never touches disk, and an explicit io.popen() refusal. Still not Lua io parity: there is no OS stream or sparse file, hard links / symlinks are outside the capability set, and binary/large-file comparisons need a real run.
features.acceptance: Compare subset against Lua, including binary/large files, mutated handles, failure and root changes; LuauIntegration.spec.cpp covers mode/seek rejection, multi-format iterators, overwrite and append positions, tmpfile, popen refusal, the byte quota and sandbox capability trimming.

features.title: Lua 5.x integer, close, goto and bytecode differences
features.gap: Delivered: source-only load is now an explicit contract - load() validates its mode (pure 'b', unknown letters and empty modes fail with a clear error), accepts 't' (including Lua's default 'bt') and always passes 't' to luaL_loadbufferx, so bytecode is never fed to Luau's source compiler nor accepted on plain Lua. Still no language-level equivalence: int64/close/goto differences, bytecode version policy and trusted-bytecode loading need an execution-backed migration contract.
features.acceptance: Publish the int64/close/goto migration contract and verify trusted bytecode; ErrorHandling.spec.cpp, LuaBackend.spec.cpp and LuaScriptCompat.spec.cpp assert mode rejection, 't'/'bt' acceptance and the env argument on both backends.

features.title: Debug service and DAP
features.gap: Full command surface delivered and verified against real state: setBreakpoints verifies each line against the resolved script's real line count; exception filters (raised/uncaught) are wired into the shared ReportLuaCallError handler, arm the line hook, stop with reason=exception and answer exceptionInfo; variables expands nested tables through registry-backed handles with depth/cycle/count budgets and releases them at the next stop or Detach. setFunctionBreakpoints matches lua_getinfo('n') names in the line hook with explicit verified=false for empty names; modules is a real package.loaded snapshot taken on the VM thread at attach and every stop, with startModule/moduleCount paging. Delivered this round: capability declarations now match the implementation - supportsFunctionBreakpoints is true (implementation, dispatch and spec already existed while the bit said false, so IDEs never sent the request), and loadedSources is implemented from that same VM-thread snapshot, resolving module names through the shared script resolver and marking unresolved entries honestly instead of inventing paths, advertised via supportsLoadedSourcesRequest. A known-unsupported command table (restart, restartFrame, terminate, stepInTargets, goto, setExpression, completions, data/instruction breakpoints, readMemory, writeMemory, disassemble, cancel, breakpointLocations, runInTerminal) returns a reason with each refusal instead of a generic 'not implemented'. Conditional / hit-conditional breakpoints, stepInTargets and restart remain declared false. launch is still an explicit refusal. Remaining: packaged remote support, authorization, reconnect and a paused-frame multi-Env/coroutine run are unverified. Runtime evidence pending.
features.acceptance: DebugAdapter.spec.cpp drives every command through a real DAP session and asserts verified breakpoints, exception capabilities/filters, function-breakpoint verification/rejection, modules paging consistency and nested-variable failure paths; it now also asserts the two newly advertised capability bits, an empty-but-successful loadedSources response while unattached, and a reasoned refusal (not a bare 'not implemented') for a known-unsupported command. DebugService.spec.cpp covers filters, last-error recording, stop reason, nested expansion refusal, function-name dedup and the package.loaded snapshot. Break/step behaviour still needs a paused-frame multi-Env/coroutine run; none of this round's C++ or automation was compiled or executed.

features.title: CPU, self time, memory and flamegraphs
features.gap: Sampled/measured attribution still differs: plain Lua pairs call/return for exact self time, Luau charges the interval between safe points to whatever was running (the GC flag is now forwarded to the profiler instead of hardcoded to 0). Delivered: lua.profiler trace on/off/reset/dump writes Luau's profile.out (relative dump paths now land under Saved/Profiling), the perfgraph.py wrapper documents an end-to-end flow and fails with an actionable submodule hint, and CN/EN console docs carry the collect -> dump -> render example. The renderer itself is upstream pinned code, so it needs the Luau submodule; stack/yield/GC attribution, overhead and malformed dumps still need execution evidence.
features.acceptance: Validate stack/yield/GC attribution, overhead and malformed dumps; follow the end-to-end example in Docs/{CN,EN}/ConsoleCommand.md and render with Tools/LuauPerfgraph/perfgraph.py once the pinned submodule is initialized.

features.title: Dead-loop and coroutine diagnostics
features.gap: Delivered: cancellation is correct and observable (GuardLeave disarms the guard that actually finished, nested guards take over the armed slot, GetTimeoutCount() counts real interruptions), plus a deterministic safe-point budget lua.maxsafepoints counted through FLuaVmHooks - LUA_MASKCOUNT instructions on plain Lua, Luau interrupts on Luau - with GetSafePointInterruptCount() and a guard that exists even when the polling thread is off. GC interrupts are passed through to listeners: the profiler uses the flag (no longer hardcoded to 0) while the watchdog and budget skip them rather than longjmp out of the collector. Delivered this round: a per-Env memory quota (lua.maxmemorykb / lua.memquota) enforced in the default allocator before every allocation, with live/peak-request/rejection counters, one actionable Error log per env on the first refusal and a recoverable VM not-enough-memory error; frees are never refused so lua_close cannot wedge, a custom lua_Alloc stays outside the quota, and ModuleContracts.spec.cpp asserts a real refusal plus VM recovery on both backends. Still not a complete hostile-code control: native callback and abandoned-coroutine attribution unproven, collector scratch allocations count towards the live waterline, and a Luau safe point is not an instruction.
features.acceptance: Test timeout/reset/teardown, nested guards, native callbacks and abandoned coroutine attribution; LuaDeadLoopCheck.spec.cpp now also asserts the safe-point budget interrupts a real loop and does not cap the next call with a stale counter. ModuleContracts.spec.cpp now asserts the quota fires, is observable and leaves the VM usable; a real dual-backend OOM/GC run is still pending.

features.title: Socket, protobuf and JSON
features.gap: Backend lifetime/ABI/error and distribution notices need component-level verification.
features.acceptance: Large/malformed payloads, socket close/failure, userdata GC and packaged linkage on both backends.

features.title: Test framework, reports and build identity
features.gap: Release orchestration, runtime manifests, strict evidence gates and provenance are implemented but unexecuted; source classification is not code coverage. Delivered this round (static only, no UE run): AuditRepository.py now validates inline AND HTML local links, Markdown anchors against MkDocs heading slugs, and plain-https remote URL syntax, and reports the historical/current-tree evidence split instead of silently counting historical runs as current coverage; ValidateRelease.py writes a schema/versioned release-gate.json carrying commit, run, backend, carrier, net_matrix and a UTC timestamp (a null commit when git is unavailable), and its showcase media gate now requires a real PNG signature and IHDR header; Tools/ValidateProvenance.py is a fail-closed static gate that keeps historical records out of current-tree coverage, checks that all four release gates (2 backends x 2 carriers) exist, are green, belong to one run and agree with release-summary.json, and can demand a non-historical record matching HEAD via --require-current. The four gate files already in the tree are legacy format with no provenance fields, so they still cannot prove they belong to the current checkout. None of this executes UE, fabricates runtime evidence or rewrites release-status.
features.acceptance: Fail missing/empty/malformed runs; record commit/dirty/dependencies/flags/topology; require type tools. Also require: python -B Tools/AuditRepository.py (links, anchors, https syntax), python -B Tools/ValidateProvenance.py --run <run> --summary <summary> --require-current (fails with 'no current-tree execution evidence' while only historical runs exist), the full Tools/tests unittest suite (185 regressions), and four freshly generated gate files whose commit matches the released HEAD. A green static structure check must never be reported as 'the current tree was verified'.

features.title: Comparable benchmarks and regression gates
features.gap: Workload contract (revision 1), UnLuaNova workload, adaptive slua-unreal/FUnLua adapter, fail-closed alignment gate and 22 static regressions delivered. Tools/CrossProject/metrics.py now produces raw multi-run distributions (min/median/mean/p95/max/stddev plus per-run medians) for one aligned project/backend, refusing mismatched hardware, project, backend, case sets or empty samples.
